content.text: No IP, deliverables, work-product, or Customer Data clause exists anywhere; ownership is asset-based and vested in the paying Parties. Submitting as compliant.

input.quote: 12.2 Parties shall obtain Allocated Capacity in the form of MIU on an ownership basis as shown in Schedule C, in return for their financial investment as identified in Schedule B.
input.rationale: This is a multi-party submarine cable construction and maintenance agreement, not a vendor supply of deliverables: the Suppliers contract separately with the Procurement Group under the Supply Contract (4.4), and there is no deliverables, work-product, licence-grant, or Customer Data ownership provision anywhere in the document. The rule's direction concern is nonetheless satisfied on its material terms. We own what we pay for outright rather than by licence: Paragraph 12.2 vests Allocated Capacity in each Party "on an ownership basis ... in return for their financial investment", Paragraph 4.1 allocates Segment ownership to the providing Parties, and Paragraph 4.3 fixes Wet Segment ownership per Schedule B. Outright ownership exceeds the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense, and our exploitation rights are unrestricted: 12.20 entitles us to sell IRU from our Allocated Capacity "on a private basis without any restrictions" and 12.22 to make it available to other Carriers "on any commercial basis without any restrictions" (the sublicensing analogue). Nothing assigns any of our intellectual property or data to the other Parties; Paragraph 31 is a mutual confidentiality regime, not a licence in our data. The common-and-undivided ownership of the Wet Segment (4.3) is the consortium bargain and is coupled with the unrestricted exploitation rights above, so it is outside the walk-away on joint ownership and benefits us. Minor points noted but not redlined: ownership runs for the Agreement term with realisation of assets under Paragraph 18 rather than being expressed as perpetual, and disclosure of APCN 2 data requires Management Committee approval (31.1) — neither is a material failure of the fallback in this asset-ownership structure.
